text:
maria: quick bakeoff recap — compared prefill (prefetching KV) vs lazy-on-demand with fp8-kv and int8-kv on the 13B-like model. observed interesting tradeoffs on cold starts and memory footprint. summary below.

devin: nice, can you post the numbers?

maria: sure. short table from the shadow runs (10k requests each):
```
Mode       | mem per instance | p50 latency | p95 latency | accuracy delta (vs fp32)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
prefill-fp8| 28GB (-38%)      | 40ms        | 120ms       | -0.9%

lazy-fp8   | 22GB (-52%)      | 45ms        | 160ms       | -1.1%

prefill-int8| 32GB (-30%)     | 42ms        | 130ms       | -0.4%

lazy-int8  | 26GB (-44%)      | 50ms        | 200ms       | -0.6%
```

maria: notes: memory delta measured vs our current fp32-kv baseline (45GB). accuracy delta is on our eval suite (QA + summarization prompts).

liam: interesting that lazy-fp8 has lower memory than prefill-fp8? typo?

maria: good catch. wording: prefill writes a compressed KV into GPU memory to avoid rebuilds on hot shards, so prefill-fp8 uses slightly more memory than lazy-fp8 in this job because prefill keeps full precomputed KV pages pinned for hot prefixes. lazy trades memory for higher p95 on first requests.

cheng: what's the cold-start behavior — do we see long tails when prefill warms from zero?

maria: prefill reduces cold-start p95 by ~40-60ms on average for heavy context sessions. but if the prefill process is stalled (I/O jitter) you can see a burst of 400–700ms while pages stream in. we instrumented and saw that on node r6c-2 during concurrent prefill.

eva: any fidelity regressions beyond the eval set? user-facing diffs?

maria: manual spot checks show occasional token-choice shifts with fp8 on long-context generation (rare hallucination style deltas). int8 appears more conservative and closer to fp32. overall pass rates: fp8 92/100, int8 97/100 on our human eval sample.

devin: ops-bot, can we get a deploy recommendation for staging canary?

ops-bot: suggested rollout: canary 3% (dedicated), monitor: model_accuracy (eval-probes), token_reject_rate, p95_latency, kv_page_faults. auto-fallback to int8-kv if model_accuracy drops >1.5% or token_reject_rate +3 sigma. :gear:

liam: I'd start with lazy-int8 on staging then a short spike of prefill-int8 to validate the warmup path. fp8 should be limited to shadow for another week.

cheng: agree. also add trace-level logging for prefill I/O; capture node id + disk latency to correlate spikes.

maria: next steps: 1) staging job: lazy-int8 canary 5% for 24h (devin) 2) shadow fp8 across 10% traffic for 48h with eval probes (eva) 3) add prefill I/O tracing (cheng) 4) prepare rollback runbook (liam). I'll post a short PR for the canary config.

eva: add an A/B prompt set that stresses long prefix reuse — that was where fp8 had the most regressions.

devin: i'll schedule the canary for tomorrow 09:00 PT. will ping when live.

maria: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
